messages:
anita: quick proposal — avoid shipping a full sidecar for private/VPC deployments by defining a minimal "probe+lease" handshake between control-plane and runtime. probe is a tiny HTTP endpoint the runtime exposes behind customer networking, returns capability set + a short-lived lease token. intent: fast capability discovery, cheaper footprint, fewer ops requirements.

marc: curious about the threat model — if we issue lease tokens, how do we prevent token replay or exfil inside VPC?

anita: two parts: 1) short TTL (30–120s) + single-use nonce optional, 2) require token binding to requestor IP or TLS client cert when available. we also keep audit logs and issue transparent rotation.

samir: KMS integration for signing leases? prefer HSM-backed signing (customers with private deployments will want that). alternatively sign with control-plane key and include signature in response so runtime can prove provenance.

anita: agree. flow sketch: control-plane -> POST /v1/leases {tenant, probe_req} signed-by-kms -> runtime accepts signed lease on probe verification. runtime keeps only lease metadata (no long-lived creds).

yuki: observability question — we need token-level telemetry without leaking tenant IDs in plaintext. propose we emit hashed tenant id + capability vector metrics. also attach span context for trace correlation.

anita: yes. metrics: `runtime.probe.success`, `runtime.probe.capabilities` (labels: quantized_capabilities), `runtime.lease.issued` and `runtime.lease.expired`. logs to configurable sink; default to control-plane audit stream.

anita: example probe interaction (illustrative):
```http
GET /v1/runtime/probe?tenant=acme-corp HTTP/1.1
Host: runtime.customer.internal
Authorization: Bearer probe-checker-key

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "capabilities": ["text-generation","streaming","kv-cache-v2"],
  "lease": "lease_3a7f...",
  "ttl_seconds": 60
}
```

anita: control-plane would issue the lease (signed) after validating connectivity and policy, the runtime honors lease for requests that map to tenant routes. runtime still enforces per-request auth — lease is admission token not replacement for full tenant auth.

marc: fallback plan if runtime doesn't expose probe (air-gapped or blocked)? we should have an offline manifest that operator can provide during install. manifests can be gzipped and verified by signature.

anita: yes — manifest fallback mode. operator can upload `hosting-manifest.json.gz` during onboarding. probe preferred for dynamic capabilities (e.g., hw accel, quantization level) but manifest used for isolated installs.

samir: tradeoffs: pros — no sidecar binary, lower ops surface, faster adoption; cons — pushes more trust into runtime TLS/certificate management, harder to transparently intercept for canarying. also we lose some local caching features a sidecar can provide.

yuki: canary idea — for a rollout, have router map 10% of probes to a sidecar-enabled runtime and compare latency/capacity vector. logs should flag capability mismatches with severity so human can triage.

anita: next steps: write short RFC with sequence diagrams, lease lifecycle, sample curl + manifest specs, and a compatibility table between probe vs sidecar (what features map to each). will schedule sync next Wed.

marc: tagging security for review: @marc please check crypto bindings and replay protection.

samir: will add KMS/HSM appendix and recommended key rotation cadence (7 days for lease keys).

infra-bot: created rfc/host-probe-lease-2026 draft in docs repo — link: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/host-probe-lease-2026

yuki: :thumbsup: sounds good. adding a checklist: (1) manifest schema, (2) lease signing spec, (3) probe telemetry labels, (4) canary plan.

anita: thanks — I'll put together the draft and drop it in the thread. any objections to calling this "probe+lease" model for naming?

marc: no objections. +1.

samir: +1

yuki: +1

anita: great — rolling into RFC writeup.
